text:
anna: quick sync 1 we need a small design decision: active/active + PII tenant shadow writes. legal flagged cross-region shadowing as a no-go unless documented consent.
marc: +1. my take: never implicitly replicate PII. put a forced opt-in consent token before any async cross-region write.
sophie: propose per-tenant flag: residency_mode = local_only | replica_with_consent | explicit_block. default local_only for sensitive scopes.
raj: ops note: replica_with_consent still means background traffic and KV cache churn. need perf budget for tail QPS and prewarm logic.
anna: routing enforcement question: should router/proxy short-circuit and deny before we hit datalayer, or let datalayer return 403 and rely on SLOs?
marc: router-level enforcement is cleaner. cheap failure, avoids cross-region serialization attempts. add a router policy check early in pipeline.
sophie: also need a header carrying consent: X-Redwood-PII-Consent: <token>. tokens TTL short (suggest 2m) and single-use idempotency hinted.
raj: can we reuse escrow service for tokens? reusing avoids new secrets but increases read load. suggest edge cache (30s) + leaky read-through to escrow.
anna: good. action items: (1) router policy API spec, (2) proxy consent token cache implementation sketch, (3) update platform docs + legal checklist.
marc: one more: audit log must surface when consent was used and which version of token; must tie to tenant-id and request-id.
sophie: and add a telemetry counter for blocked-by-residency to help compliance reports.
raj: ops addendum  we should simulate worst-case QPS in staging with a high mix of replica_with_consent tenants.
deploy-bot: deploy/patch-4721 applied to staging: feature flag residency_proxy_enforce = on. :white_check_mark:
